senses.gloss: (v. עִילָה) [round about way,] circumvention, perverseness, insidiousness; pretext, false charge.
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 101b:3">Snh. 101ᵇ</cite> <he>שלשה באו בע׳</he> three men (Biblical personages) came with indirectness (instead of praying in a straightforward manner).

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 93:12">Gen. R. s. 93</cite> <he>מתחלה באת עלינו בע׳</he> from the start thou camest against us with insidiousness (trying to find charges against us); Tanḥ. Vayigg. 5; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 151:2">Yalk. Gen. 151</cite>.
<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 7:13">Esth. R. to III, 9</cite> <he>המן</he> … <he>בע׳ גדולה וכ׳</he> Haman, the wicked, came with great trickery against Israel (tempting them to sin).
<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 7:13">Ib.</cite> <he>באו בע׳ וכ׳</he> they (the Israelites) came with a pretext, saying, let us go to sacrifice (<cite ref="Exodus 5:3">Ex. V, 3</cite>).

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 26:1">Pesik. R. s. 26</cite> <he>ראה היאך תמצא לו ע׳ וכ׳</he> see how thou canst find a charge against Jeremiah and be revenged on him; a. fr.—Pl. as ab. Ex. R. l. c., v. <cite ref="P00376"><he>עָוַת</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 20:8">Num. R. s. 20</cite> <he>שלא ליתן לו ע׳</he> (not <he>יתן</he>) so as not to allow him any excuses.
